It features a public area for discovering models and a protected area for submission and curation, governed by a formal curation policy to maintain quality and standardization.

generalInfo.name: PLANTdataHUB
generalInfo.provider: University of Freiburg
generalInfo.description: The PLANTdataHUB platform provides a resource, enabling modern RDM for the plant community with state-of-the art knowledge organization. It combines existing free and open-source platforms and standards to store and organizes ARCs in a central repository. Moreover, it supports ARCs with facilities for automated quality control, data interrogation, and collaboration workflows. PLANTdataHUB is also a software-as-a-service blueprint, and instances can be realized at any level (personal, institutional, or global) that is convenient for the supported research process, while retaining full interoperability with the central instance and each other. In this manuscript, we describe the architecture of the PLANTdataHUB and explore the design choices underlying it.

generalInfo.name: ARChive
generalInfo.provider: University of Freiburg
generalInfo.description: The ARChive (archive.nfdi4plants.org) is the central, open-access data publication and long-term storage repository for the German plant science research community. Operating under the DataPLANT consortium (part of Germany's National Research Data Infrastructure, NFDI), it is designed specifically for publishing data formatted as Annotated Research Contexts (ARCs). ARCs are self-contained digital packages that seamlessly tie together raw experimental omics data (genomics, metabolomics, proteomics, phenomics), detailed metadata, and the exact computational workflows used to analyze them. Built using the open-source InvenioRDM framework, the ARChive features an automated "Continuous Quality Control" (CQC) validation pipeline. This ensures that submitted datasets adhere to strict international metadata standards (like ISA, CWL, and MIAPPE) and auto-mints persistent Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs), turning traditional static biological archives into highly reproducible, actionable, and machine-readable assets.

generalInfo.name: LIMSOPHY
generalInfo.provider: Leibniz Institut for Plant Genetics and Crop Plant Research (IPK)
generalInfo.description: LIMSOPHY at IPK is an enterprise-grade Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) and relational data back-end framework customized specifically for the unique workflows of crop science. Implemented at the Leibniz Institute of Plant Genetics and Crop Plant Research (IPK), it serves as a central digital archive that structures and integrates vast layers of heterogeneous research assets. The platform tracks over 4,000 distinct plant experiments, logs nearly 2.5 million biological probes and material tracking points, and houses upwards of 14 million raw data records—including automated calculation formulas, phenotypic time-series imaging captured by high-throughput LemnaTec systems, and historical genebank passport photographs. By utilizing a customized commercial core from AAC Infotray AG, it reliably connects disparate laboratory data silos while providing programmatic access via the FAIR-IPK REST API to ensure data reproducibility.

generalInfo.name: Semantic Lookup Platform
generalInfo.provider: Leibniz Institute of Plant Biochemistry (IPB Halle)
generalInfo.description: SemLookP is a semantic lookup and ontology integration service supporting FAIR metadata annotation and search in the life sciences. It is built on the EBI Ontology Lookup Service (OLS) and Ontology Xref (OxO) mapping tool. SemLookP provides access to key standardized ontologies for annotating human, mouse and rat omics data and clinical data, and includes terminologies for genes, gene variants, transcripts (mRNAs/miRNAs), and proteins. A mapping service connects concepts across different vocabularies, allowing researchers to semantically annotate data and literature in an unambiguous, interoperable way
generalInfo.Type_of_resources_present: Standardized terminologies/ontologies (controlled vocabularies in health and chemistry domains) and their cross-reference mappings. SemLookP’s public instance includes major biomedical vocabularies (e.g. SNOMED CT, ICD) and domain ontologies like FoodEx2/FOODON for nutrition, etc., plus mappings between equivalent terms across these resources
generalInfo.License: Varied by source ontology. Ontologies accessible via SemLookP are subject to their individual licenses: many are open (e.g. CC BY or CC0 for public ontologies like FOODON), while some medical terminologies (e.g. SNOMED CT, ICD) have restricted or proprietary licensing

generalInfo.description: SoilWise HE (soilwise-he.eu) is an open-access European data and knowledge repository funded by the Horizon Europe "Mission Soil" project, designed to safeguard and improve soil health by 2030. It functions as an integrated, actionable hub that brings together scattered, mismatched soil datasets from across Europe, making them Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) for researchers, farmers, and policymakers. By utilizing machine learning, AI-driven natural language processing, and integrated knowledge graphs, the platform harmonizes heterogeneous data—such as soil erosion, carbon sequestration, and contaminant metrics—to provide a reliable infrastructure for data-driven spatial policies and informed decision-making.
